title: Windows automation probe — WIN20's WinUI 3 plane witness
note: WIN20's own probe window, not the product. Kept as a surface because it is what proves the automation plane works at all, and because its two SecondaryCommands are the recorded unoracled pair: a CommandBar's overflow items are not realised while the overflow is closed, so they exist on neither the control view nor the raw view.

title: Windows shell — NavigationView, caption band, title, menus
note: WIN3. The shell is ONE surface and its ten destinations are ten more, per the destination-collapse rule. Navigation was verified honest 2026-09-02: DestinationCatalog declares 10 destinations and ShellWindow.SelectDestination maps 10 distinct board types, with BoardPlaceholder reachable only as the unknown-id fallback.

title: Windows Servers board and the Signal Path
Windows Activity board — the live call log
Windows Skills board
note: WIN6. One literal control name in XAML; the rest are built in DataTemplates and code-behind, so the declared list is a floor and the UIA tree is the census.

title: Windows Checks board
note: WIN8. Both declared names are STATES rather than controls; the board's real affordances are per-row and templated. Recorded as-is so the gap is visible rather than papered over.

title: Windows Cleanup board
note: WIN9. `Remove selected…` is a destructive control — any sweep touching this board runs under the write firewall, never against a live config.

title: Windows Inbox board and review sheet
note: WIN10. The three tab labels carry counts, so their accessible names move with the data — a case matching them exactly will be brittle by construction and must match on role plus prefix.

title: Windows Settings board
note: WIN13 claims 7 sections and Fluent ToggleSwitch controls; the XAML declares exactly ONE literal control name. Either the toggles carry no AutomationProperties.Name — which is an accessibility defect and makes them unaddressable from the automation plane — or there are fewer than claimed. The UIA dump settles which, and this note stays until it does.

title: Windows ambient surface — notification-area flyout
note: WIN11. Not a destination and not addressable by a route: it is raised from the notification area. Reaching it needs an actuation the self-test driver does not perform, so it is `manual` rather than `ready` — counted, with the reason, rather than absent.

title: Windows pairing dialog
note: WIN12. A ContentDialog reached from the Inbox board's `Pair iPhone…`. One literal control name; the pairing code and countdown are templated.

title: Windows capability document panel — three tabs over one package
note: WIN16. Reached from Skills, Discover or Inbox rather than from the shell's own navigation.

title: Windows Discover detail dialog
note: WIN7's detail dialog. DiscoverDetailContent.xaml declares NO literal control name and no AutomationProperties.Name at all, so nothing on it is addressable from the automation plane by name. That is a finding, and it is why the control list is empty rather than omitted.
